title: offline operator bundle validation and rollback notes
content:
Purpose and scope:

This note captures a compact, operationally-oriented playbook for validating offline/operator bundles for air-gapped Redwood Private installs, plus a conservative rollback strategy for in-place operator upgrades. It is intentionally prescriptive and checklist-driven so SREs and solutions engineers can run a predictable validation matrix before handing an upgrade bundle to a customer.

Scope: operator-based installs (Kubernetes), bundle contains: container image tarballs, Helm/OLM bundles, CRD schema files, tfstate-compatible artifact manifests, and an optional dependency tarball (python wheels, UN*X binaries). Does not cover full infra provisioning or network design.

Pre-reqs (on host used to curate and validate bundle):
- Linux workstation/container with at least 50GB free disk and Docker/podman installed.
- sha256sum, gpg (or cosign), jq, skopeo, oc/ kubectl, helm, operator-sdk (if OLM integration), yq.
- A canonical `bundle-manifest.yaml` (example schema below) and the mirror directory tree created under /tmp/airgap-mirror/<bundle-id>.
- Terraform module interface contract: see TF notes section.

Bundle manifest (minimal schema):
- bundle-id: string
- version: semver
- created_by: user
- images: [ {image: "registry.example.com/redwood/runtime:1.4.2", digest: "sha256:...", file: "images/runtime-1.4.2.tar"} ]
- charts: [ {name: "redwood-console", version: "0.9.0", file: "charts/redwood-console-0.9.0.tgz"} ]
- crds: ["manifests/crd-*.yaml"]
- extras: ["wheels/rdw-optimizer-0.2.1.whl"]
- checksums: map of file->sha256
- signature: optional detached signature (cosign/gpg)

Signing & verification policy:
- All official bundles must be signed with the release key (cosign preferred). Include detached signature at /signatures/<bundle-id>.sig.
- Verification step must be automated in the validation harness: cosign verify-blob --signature <sig> <manifest>.
- If customer operates a different trust model, document their fingerprint and include a verification step in the delivered runbook.

Image mirroring guidance (authoritative workflow):
1) Use skopeo to copy images into a local registry mirror (recommended) OR prepare saved tarballs with podman save/docker save as shipped artifacts. Example command to validate digest: skopeo inspect docker://registry.example.com/redwood/runtime:1.4.2 | jq -r '.Digest'
2) Save image files named exactly as in manifest, verify sha256: sha256sum images/runtime-1.4.2.tar | cut -d ' ' -f1 -> compare to manifest checksums.
3) For local registry: load images and re-tag to the customer local registry host/path then push. For tarball installs: provide documented load steps using ctr/podman/docker.

Operator bundle curation checklist:
- [ ] CRDs present and pinned to exact file versions (no Kustomize overlays left unresolved).
- [ ] CRD versions checked against both old and new operator to detect incompatible schema changes.
- [ ] Helm/OLM metadata contains CSV/annotations with "replaces" field set for upgrades where appropriate.
- [ ] Images referenced by the operator manifest are present in images/ and checksums match.
- [ ] All images are mirrored to a separate test mirror and then re-referenced with new registry host in a validation cluster.
- [ ] Migration jobs (if any) are bundled as separate job images and documented with a timeout and idempotency notes.

Validation harness (recommended lightweight steps):
- Step 0: unpack bundle and run manifest quick-check: yq eval '.images | length' bundle-manifest.yaml to ensure images list not empty.
- Step 1: create fresh test cluster (KinD or ephemeral customer-like VPC cluster) matching customer's k8s minor version.
- Step 2: configure local imagePullSecrets / registry mirror to use mirrored images.
- Step 3: apply CRDs first: kubectl apply -f manifests/crds/ --server-side=false
- Step 4: install operator (helm/olm) with elevated debug logging. Wait on operator pod readiness (kubectl -n redwood wait --for=condition=available deployment/redwood-operator --timeout=10m).
- Step 5: exercise basic reconciliation: create a minimal custom resource (CR) and validate operator created expected child resources. Capture logs and events.
- Step 6: run upgrade path in validation cluster if this is an upgrade bundle: install older operator version, create canonical CR set, then apply new bundle and observe migration behavior.

Terraform module interface notes (for packaging bootstrap and mirror automation):
- Input vars (minimum): bundle_id (string), mirror_path (string, local path or remote s3-like uri), registry_host (string), image_rewrite_map (map of original->mirror), install_method ("tarball"|"registry"), cluster_kubeconfig (string path).
- Outputs: bundle_manifest_s3_url (string), validation_report_path (string), rollback_marker (string).
- Important: module must not attempt to mutate cluster state in the air-gapped customer's control plane. It should produce artifacts and an installation plan file that the customer executes.
- Provide an optional `tfplan` target that emits a `bundle_install_plan.json` which contains deterministic steps (apply CRDs, import images, install helm).

Upgrade plan (conservative, in-place operator upgrade):
1) Pre-upgrade snapshot: capture all operator CRs and relevant namespaces (kubectl get <CR> -o yaml > pre-upgrade/). Export cluster resource read-only snapshot for quick restore if needed.
2) Dry-run in canary cluster (exactly mirrored images and configs). Run upgrade and validate.
3) Schedule maintenance window and increase observability TTLs.
4) Install new operator in "replaces" mode if supported otherwise side-by-side with new namespace and test controllers.
5) Run operator-provided migration jobs with low concurrency; monitor metrics for error increases.
6) If any blocking error is detected (see gating thresholds below), trigger rollback.

Rollback policy and concrete steps (fast safe path):
- Gate thresholds that should abort an upgrade: >1% of CRs failing final state after N minutes, pod crashloop backoff rate > 3 within 15 minutes, new operator not reaching Ready after 10m.
- Fast rollback steps (to be run by SRE/solutions):
  a) Apply the saved manifests from pre-upgrade snapshot for CRs and operator deployment.
  b) If new images introduced DB migrations that are not reversible, run database restore from customer-provided snapshot (this must be planned ahead).
  c) Re-tag images to old digests in local registry and re-deploy old operator deployment.
  d) Mark rollback-marker in bundle storage so automation can skip re-attempts without manual signoff.
- Post-rollback validation: run a smoke test that exercises the top 5 customer-critical flows for 10 minutes and produce a short report.

Automated checks and sample commands (copy/paste friendly):
- Verify all checksums: for f in $(jq -r '.checksums | keys[]' bundle-manifest.json); do echo $f; sha256sum $f | awk '{print $1}'; done
- Validate images digest in tarball: skopeo inspect --raw docker-archive:images/runtime-1.4.2.tar | jq -r '.Config' >/dev/null || echo "bad image"
- Quick CRD compatibility check: kubeval --kubernetes-version=$K8S_VER manifests/crds/*.yaml || true

Known failure modes and mitigations:
- Missing image tags in manifest: fail early, mandate digest presence.
- CRD incompatible change (remove field): include an automated diff step between old/new CRD schemas and flag potential destructive changes.
- Registry TTL/timeouts on customer's local registry: include retry/backoff and a mirrored tarball fallback path.

Deliverable runbook snippet to hand to customer (concise):
- Unpack bundle, verify signature, verify checksums.
- Load images: for each images/*.tar -> podman load -i <file> && podman tag -> push to local registry.
- Apply CRDs, then install operator helm chart pointing to local registry.
- Run smoke CR and validate expected status==Ready within 10m.

Appendix: quick test matrix (minimal to run before shipping bundle)
- Platform matrix: k8s 1.22, 1.23, 1.24 (test at least the major customer target).
- Operator lifecycle paths: fresh install, upgrade from N-1, upgrade from N-2 (if supported), rollback from N+1->N.
- Artifacts: images checksum pass, manifest signature verified, charts render (helm template) without unresolved values.

Notes & open questions:
- Decide standard for migration job timeouts (30m vs 2h) per customer class.
- Make a small reusable validation container image (rdw-airgap-validator:latest) that contains the harness and common binary tools. This will reduce local dependency drift when solutions engineers validate bundles.

If this doc looks good we should fold core snippets into the airgap-scripts repo and create a small TF wrapper that emits the `bundle_install_plan.json` described above.

Revision history: Drafted by Marisol Vega 2025-02-10; edits by Ari Kaplan 2025-02-22 (added TF interface notes); Linh Tran 2025-03-02 (clarified rollback gating thresholds).
